title: Alkanes, fuels and cracking
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR06#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t4 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR06#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR06#N.4, OR06#N.11, OR06#N.14, OR06#N.17.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Soot
items.clue: The solid C that can form when an alkane burns in limited oxygen.

items.label: Haemoglobin
items.clue: Binds CO more strongly than oxygen, so the blood carries less oxygen.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Toxic gas with no smell, formed when an alkane burns in limited oxygen.

items.label: Incomplete combustion
items.clue: Burning of an alkane in limited oxygen, giving CO and/or C as well as H₂O.

questions.stem: Which alkane has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Longest chain and unbranched: most electrons and most surface contact, so the strongest forces between molecules (bp 69 °C).

questions.stem: Methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen. Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon is deposited as soot, while the hydrogen still forms water. 1 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Which pollutant in car exhaust forms from the air rather than from the fuel?
questions.explanation: Air is mostly N₂ and O₂. At the high temperature inside an engine they combine: N₂ + O₂ → 2NO. The fuel contains no nitrogen.

questions.stem: A gas heater burns methane in a small room. The window is shut and the air vent is blocked. Why is this dangerous?

options.text: Methane burns completely, and the carbon dioxide that forms is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so CO forms, which cuts the oxygen that blood can carry.
Oxygen runs short, so unburned methane builds up, and methane is a poison.
Oxygen runs short, so the hydrogen in methane escapes as poisonous hydrogen gas.

questions.explanation: Limited oxygen gives incomplete combustion. CO binds to haemoglobin more strongly than O₂ does. It has no colour or smell.
